newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CAPELLO UNDER FIRE AGAIN AS "BORING" REAL SLIP UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAPELLO UNDER FIRE AGAIN AS "BORING" REAL SLIP UP.

text.p: Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello has walked into another storm of criticism after his side could only manage a goalless draw against Logrones -- a team that Barcelona had beaten 8-0.
"Boring" read a headline in the "As" newspaper. "What a horror" was the front page comment in another sports daily, 'Marca'.

And on a weekend when Barcelona proved they could play without Brazilian striker Ronaldo, Real showed their complete dependence on Predrag Mijatovic and Davor Suker, who scored vital World Cup goals for Yugoslavia and Croatia respectively.
"With what we have, it can't be done better," said Capello after the game. "At least we haven't lost a game."

After successive goalless draws in the Santiago Bernabeu stadium, both Capello, in his first season at Madrid after joining the club from AC Milan in the summer, and club president Lorenzo Sanz agree that Real need to look for new players when the Spanish transfer market re-opens in December.
Even so Sanz was quick to remind reporters that around five billion pesetas was spent on reinforcements in the close season.
"More than one coach would like this squad," said Sanz.
To make matters worse, injury-prone Argentine midfielder Fernando Redondo hurt his finger during the game and is likely to be out for at least ten days.
One curious anecdote to emerge from the match was Andoni Cedrun's sprinkling of garlic around his goalmouth.
The Logrones keeper -- who had let in 14 goals in his previous away games -- relied on a traditional Mediterranean method of keeping away evil spirits. At least that seemed to work.
